def: A pair of adjacent characters used as an index term, so scripts written without spaces can be searched without a dictionary.
A tokeniser that cuts unspaced text into real words using a dictionary and statistics, such as MeCab for Japanese or jieba for Chinese.
A writing system such as Latin, Arabic, Han or Thai, which Unicode records for every character.
Classifying which language a piece of text is written in, unreliable on very short strings and on closely related languages.
The order in which text is read and stored, as opposed to the left-to-right order in which its glyphs are drawn on screen.
The Unicode algorithm (UAX #9) that turns text stored in logical order into the display order of mixed left-to-right and right-to-left runs.
Unicode code points for the shaped glyphs of connected scripts such as Arabic, which PDFs often store instead of the base letters and which NFKC maps back.
Finding documents in one language with a query in another, using a multilingual embedder or translation.
The tendency of a multilingual retriever to rank documents in the query's own language above equally relevant documents in other languages.
The Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark, covering over 500 tasks across more than 250 languages.
